newsitem.title: UK: Mercury says new clients to keep old numbers.
newsitem.headline: Mercury says new clients to keep old numbers.

text.p: Mercury Communications, the local subsidiary of UK telecoms group Cable and Wireless, said on Thursday that customers would soon be able to connect directly to its network without having to change telephone numbers.

After sealing an agreement with telecoms giant British Telecommunications, which still connects more than 90 percent of the residential telephone market, Mercury said it was the first national operator to offer "number portability".
"Number portability will liberate customers and enable them to move to whichever company offers the best service for them," said Mercury's strategy director Christopher Weston.

Customers, who have invested money marketing and promoting their telephone numbers have been reluctant to change supplier because they are afraid of losing the goodwill of their clients as well as incurring the costs of reprinting marketing material.
"This agreement removes one of the main barriers faced by consumers wishing to take advantage of alternative suppliers' products and services," Weston added in a statement.

Mercury plans to introduce "single-line geographic number portability" early next month for customers in Northern Ireland, rolling out the programme nationally in 1997. This only affects clients who have, for example, kept a fax line with a BT number.
But this paves the way for the introduction of a multi-line geographic number portability service which will also be rolled out nationally in 1997, Mercury said.
Large customers will then be able to change supplier without changing telephone numbers.

Mercury, the second biggest telecoms player in the UK, said it was also working with industry regulator Oftel and other telecoms groups to trial and launch number portability services that have no geographic significance -- for example toll-free services, such as 0800 and 0500 calls, and toll-shared services.
Trials with BT begin next May.
